newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rose on strong fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rose on strong fundamentals.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed slightly higher Thursday after a soft opening, boosted once again by high hopes for the local economy, traders said.
"The stock market showed a very strong move," said Luis Corsiglia, analyst at Corsiglia brokers.
Traders said the market fell at the opening on the poor health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.

But the market rose in the afternoon as "the economy continues to pick up, there are more sectors recovering and the firm decision by President (Carlos) Menem to go on with his reforms," said Corsiglia.
The Merval leading blue-chip stock index slipped to 580 points early but closed at 584.61, 0.25 percent higher than Wednesday's close.
Traders underlined the importance to the market of finishing another week with advances.

"If the market ends higher on the week again, it will be seventh week with a rise, which is important because the last time we had a 10-week increase, we hit record highs in December 1993," said another analyst. "That can only happen with the help of fundamentals."
Volume rose to $15.9 million, up from $14.6 million Wednesday.
Fourteen stocks rose, 23 declined and 23 were unchanged.
The main gainers were metal maker Acindar, which rose 5.2 percent, automaker Sevel which gained 4.0 percent and textile company Alpargatas, which advanced 1.5 percent.
Among the largest decliners were oil company Sol Petroleo, which dropped 2.5 percent, and paper and pulp company Celulosa, which fell 2.3 percent.
